instruction: Write a first-touch outbound email for Vercel that sounds like a strong SDR, not a marketing sequence. Lead with one grounded trigger. In the first sentence, reference the trigger directly, or if the trigger is anonymized internal intent, open with the operational question it usually implies instead of exposing tracking details. In the next sentence, connect that trigger to one concrete Vercel-relevant outcome such as cleaner preview workflow, release coordination, migration risk reduction, or developer velocity. End with one low-friction CTA offering a useful artifact or a short compare-notes conversation. Keep the body between 70 and 120 words. Stay plainspoken, specific, and commercially useful. Use one primary signal and at most one supporting detail. No generic pleasantries, no hype, no long social proof, no bullet lists, no multiple asks, and no Calendly-first CTA. The subject should be specific to the trigger and usually 4 to 8 words.
summary: BootstrapFewShot-style deployed prompt. Four high-performing historical v2 examples are appended as few-shot demos. The live instruction teaches one grounded trigger, one operational implication, and one low-friction CTA in plainspoken SDR language.

demos.leadContext: Rita Alvarez is Head of Web Platform at OrbitIQ. Play: Migration Watch. Top signal: App-router migration: Core routes moved from CRA to Next.js. Why now: Migration commits accelerated this month and deployment choices are next. Confidence: Concrete migration activity.

topSignal.label: App-router migration
topSignal.value: Core routes moved from CRA to Next.js.

draft.subject: OrbitIQ migration: deployment checklist
draft.body:
Hi Rita,

Saw OrbitIQ move key repos from CRA to Next.js recently. Teams usually hit the same friction right after this step: cache policy, preview discipline, and environment parity.

Happy to share a short migration checklist if useful.

— Alex
